messages:
incident-bot: Pager: SRE-PAGE triggered for api.redwood.com - elevated 5xx and TLS handshake failures reported across multiple edge POPs. Severity: P1. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/edge-cf-tls|edge-cf-tls>. Link to alert: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/87423

sara: I'm the on-call. jumping in. seeing a mix of 525 (SSL handshake failed) and 502 from Cloudflare edges, across eu-west and us-east. Not seeing origin errors yet.

mike: Confirmed from metrics. edge_handshake_failures spike at 2113456400, latency slightly up. Quick curl shows handshake failures:
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.com/health
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
* SSL: certificate verification error: unable to get local issuer certificate
* Closing connection 0
< HTTP/1.1 525 SSL Handshake Failed
```
Not origin timeouts - tcpdump between origin and our LB looks normal.

kevin: I'm checking Cloudflare status. There's an incident note for certain POPs: https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/xyq7k - seems to match eu and parts of us-east.

ana (ana): Heads-up on customer impact: Hosted API customers in EU seeing increased errors (~3-8%) and some control-plane calls failing for the console. We've had two support tickets reporting "API errors when saving settings". No billing systems affected.

mike: Start mitigation attempt 1: shift CF load balancer weights away from affected POPs / regions. Executing patch to LB to reduce eu POP weight to 0 and increase us-west to handle more traffic. Command I'm running: 
```
curl -X PATCH "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/<ZONE>/load_balancers/<LB_ID>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CF_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"default_pools":["us-west-pool"], "fallback_pool":"us-west-pool"}'
```
Applied now, CF reports 200. Propagation ~30s.

ops_jun: I deployed the LB change. traffic to eu pool weight set to 0. Watching.

sara: Monitoring metrics - error rate for EU decreased from ~6% to ~2.3% over the last 90s. Some customers still see TLS handshake failures routed via partner CDNs (we're seeing variability).

kevin: Opened an urgent support ticket with Cloudflare and escalated to on-call: Ticket CF-2113459 (link: https://support.cloudflare.com/tickets/CF-2113459). They acknowledge "edge handshake regressions in specific POPs" and are investigating SNI/TLS termination.

mike: As a temporary fallback for severely impacted customers, we have a plan to add CNAME failover to our secondary CDN/origin pair. That requires DNS changes (low TTL already set). If CF can't restore POPs quickly we may cut a partial DNS-level failover for a subset of traffic. Not doing that yet - coordinating with product.

ana (ana): Drafted customer comms: "We're investigating intermittent API errors impacting some EU users. We're mitigating by shifting traffic away from affected edge locations and working with our provider. We'll update in 30 minutes or on resolution." Ready to send to impacted account list after you confirm.

mike: Also tried toggling one experimental TLS flag from the edge per the CF guidance (disabled TLS 1.3 experimental on the domain) to test impact. No obvious improvement yet. Rolling that back to avoid client-side regressions.

ops_jun: Cloudflare telemetry shows degraded TLS success rate at those POPs. They're redeploying edge configs right now.

sara: Error rate trending down further to ~1.1% across EU. Will keep LB weights in place for now. Keeping runbook step 5 (open ticket, shift weights) as completed.

lisa: Taking over oncall at 21:05 UTC. Handoff: mitigation applied (LB weights), ticket CF-2113459 open and escalated, customer comm draft ready, current impact reduced but not fully resolved. I'll monitor for next 6hrs and revert LB weights only after CF confirms POPs healthy. Links: runbook, dashboards, ticket.

incident-bot: Incident status update: severity downgraded to P2 based on impact reduction. Next update expected in 30m or on change.
